name: Abel Tasman Coast Track
why: Coastal forest and golden bays from Mārahau to Tōtaranui, with tidal estuaries to wade and a water taxi back.
book: Huts and campsites must be booked all year round. Mārahau is 18 km from Motueka; book the water taxi back from Tōtaranui. Check the tide tables: Awaroa Inlet can only be crossed 1 h 30 min before to 2 h after low tide.
water: Tap water at huts and campsites, untreated: boil or treat it.
dangers: Awaroa Inlet is a compulsory tidal crossing: arrive at the wrong time and you wait hours.
Steep, rough or muddy sections between the bays.
Sun on the beaches and sandflies at the campsites.
turnaround: At Awaroa, if low tide does not fit your day, stay at Awaroa Hut or take the water taxi from Awaroa beach.

points.name: Mārahau
points.note: Track start at the park entrance; the causeway crosses the estuary.

points.name: Anchorage Hut
points.note: First night, 12.4 km in, on the beach of Anchorage Bay. Te Pukatea Bay is over the hill.

points.name: Bark Bay Hut
points.note: Second night. On the way, the 47 m Falls River bridge; Torrent Bay estuary has an all-tide track.

points.name: Awaroa Hut
points.note: Third night on Awaroa Inlet, after Onetahuti Bay and Tonga Saddle. Cross the inlet at low tide.

points.name: Tōtaranui
points.note: Ranger office, campground and beach, 7.1 km past the inlet. Water taxis back to Mārahau.
